Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J29/J29nB239.xml). Chuiwan Guangzhen discusses Linji's three mysteries and three essentials and warns against looking for their point in inherited formulations. He explicitly introduces an older verse by Juefan, reciting the full sequence whose closing couplet is the headword. Chuiwan uses it to test whether readers understand the three errors in taking such phrases literally. The exact couplet is quoted Juefan, not Chuiwan's new poem.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J39/J39nB466.xml). Baishan Dekai's record says his doubt about the three mysteries intensified after a teacher rebuked him. When a rice ladle falls and bounces, he suddenly awakens and recites the headword couplet with a laugh. He then remarks that an older elder had spoken this way. Baishan voices the words in his own awakening scene while explicitly acknowledging a prior speaker; this is reuse, not proof of Baishan's original authorship.

Senses.Explanation: Juefan's deliberately impossible image of a stone woman's hair standing in a dream marks the breakdown of calculating thought in a verse on Linji's three mysteries and three essentials. Chuiwan Guangzhen explicitly quotes the older Juefan's verse while warning that treating Linji's three mysteries and three essentials as fixed formulas misses their living use. Hanyue Fazang cites the same verse in a letter and explains its images as a move beyond contrived understanding. Chaozong Tongren repeats Juefan's closing lines in a long criticism of how that earlier teacher interpreted Linji's categories. Those three sources are quotations or arguments about one verse. Guxue Zhenzhe uses its closing couplet as his own immediate reply when monks fail his challenge about a pair of plums and one asks him to answer instead. In Baishan Dekai's awakening account, a falling rice ladle resolves a long doubt over the mysteries; he spontaneously recites the same couplet, then acknowledges an older elder who had said it. The later direct uses show how the verse became a ready expression for an encounter that defeats planned speech, without making those teachers its first composer.

Occurrences.Kwic: 火一夕而燼，大眾譁譟動山谷，而黃龍安坐如平時。桂林僧洪準欲掖之而走，顧見叱之，準曰：和尚縱厭世間，慈明法道何所賴耶？因徐整衣起，而火已及座榻矣。坐是入獄，郡吏發其私忿，考掠百至，絕口不言，唯不食而已。兩月而後得釋，鬚髮不剪，皮骨僅存。真點胸迎於中塗，見之不自知，泣下曰：師兄何至是也？黃龍叱曰：者俗漢！真不覺拜之。蓋其不動如山類如此。曹山躭章禪師初辭洞山悟本，本曰：吾在雲巖先師處親印寶鏡三昧，事窮的要，今付受汝。汝善護持，無令斷絕，遇真法器，方可傳委。直須秘密，不得影露，恐屬流布，喪滅吾宗。夫末法時代，人多乾慧，若要辨認向去之人真偽，有三種滲漏，當機直須具眼：一、見滲漏者，機不離位，墮在毒海；二、情滲漏者，智常向背，見處偏枯；三、語滲漏者，體妙失宗，機昧終始，濁智流轉。於此三種，子宜知之。又綱要三偈，初敲倡俱行，曰：金針雙鎻備，狹路隱全該，寶印當空妙，重重錦縫開。其次金鎻玄路，曰：交牙明中暗，功齊轉覺難，力窮尋進退，金鎻網鞔鞔。又其次理事俱不涉，曰：理事俱不涉，回照絕幽微，背風無巧拙，電火爍難追。衲子當機，能如電火難追，則方透三種滲漏。圓覺曰：眾生為解礙，菩薩未離覺。故知脫生死於言下，自非上根大智，何以臻此？大愚以黃檗為老婆，良有以也。黃檗每曰：決定不流至第二念，就中方入我宗門。盖宗乘有旨趣，下流不悟，妄生同異，欲望大法之興，不亦難乎？

Senses.Explanation: To have a discerning eye is to be able to recognize, distinguish, or judge what an encounter presents. Yuanwu Keqin contrasts a genuinely discerning participant with blind guidance. Dongshan Liangjie tells Caoshan Benji that one must be discerning at the moment of engagement. Weilin Daopei grants the description to someone who can distinguish two answers. Muzhou Daoming tests a donor’s discernment, Sanshan Lai describes a discerning guide, and Mingjue Cong uses the expanded forehead-eye form. These are public tests and attributions of discernment, not descriptions of physical eyesight.

Senses.Explanation: To be complete, fully endowed, or lacking nothing. Xuansha says, “each person is fully endowed; each person is manifest” (人人具足，人人成現). Another address ranges across monastics and laypeople, women and men, wise and foolish, noble and low, saying all are fully endowed “without the least lacking” (悉皆具足，曾無欠少). Hongzhi pairs “fully endowed from the beginning” (本來具足) with “not a hair's breadth lacking, not a hair's breadth in excess.” A later text warns that merely accepting “fully endowed from the beginning, no need to seek outside” can become empty talk. In the ordination compound “full precepts” (具足戒), the same completeness word modifies the precepts: biographies record receiving or being given the full precepts. Predicate and attributive placement express the same completeness, not different lexical referents.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Fully present as an ordinary person, yet unaware; fully present as a sage, yet not conceiving it
SearchAliases: fully present as an ordinary person, yet unaware; fully present as a sage, yet not conceiving it
Senses.Note: The pair says an ordinary person is complete in ordinary person’s reality without knowing it, while a sage is complete in sage’s reality without conceiving it. Miyun and Feiyin use it to unsettle a fixed border between the two. Baichi brings it into the street and market; Baiyu strikes his knees while asking which is which. The paired saying tests how people make and undo the distinction in the present.

Senses.Note: Longji Shaoxiu balances two claims: ordinary people have the ordinary person's way without knowing it, and sages have the sage's way without comprehending it. Tianyin asks his assembly whether they know the distinction, while Feiyin applies both sides to each person's present capacity. Yun'e challenges Longji's apparent exchange of poor and rich; Fangrong sets knowing aside and demands to see what is complete. Hongzhi says even a fully worked out answer must be released. The headword keeps the sage half of a deliberately reversible pair in view.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J36/J36nB363.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Wenmunian. Wenmu Nian sets Hao’s verse against a later Jianfu remark and appraises both in his present discourse.

Senses.Explanation: Three recorded-saying teachers use Yuquan Hao’s old loincloth verse to test claims about hardship and practice. Baichi quotes Hao’s red-cloth verse and answers by changing the cloth to white, making his response turn on a different image of wear. Guantao Qi cites the same old verse in a separate teaching and questions whether displaying such poverty really amounts to the point of practice. Wenmu Nian raises Hao’s line again, sets it beside a later Jianfu remark, and gives his own appraisal of both. The identical old verse is a common target; each present teacher performs a distinct criticism.

Senses.Explanation: The question presses continuity between immeasurable past time and the present moment. Huiyue Xu ends his own evening verse by asking how all past ages differ from today. Gumei Dinglie quotes the older line and immediately asks his assembly whether they recognize the matter of this very day. Fayan Wenyi attributes it to Bao Gong and explains it through ordinary acts such as dressing, eating, and moving about. Ruibai Mingxue uses it in his own verse about a mountain stone that endures sun and wind. These scenes bring the long span of time into a present image or task.

Senses.Explanation: Distinctly clear describes what the records present as individually evident rather than blurred or hidden. Linji Yixuan applies it to the person listening before his eyes; other records apply it to mountains, water, bird calls, buildings, bells, a spoken line, or brightness. It can stand alone or be reinforced by phrases meaning 'brightly clear,' 'clearly distinct,' or 'solitary brightness.' The expression reports distinctness; the surrounding noun or clause identifies what is clear.

Senses.Explanation: The ocean-seal complete command is an all-at-once seal or display in which differences appear without obstructing one another. The records define, invoke, and question its power rather than leaving it as an untranslated title. An ocean reflecting and receiving many streams becomes the seal by which many appearances are displayed or fixed without losing their differences. The witnesses describe its operation differently; the entry reports those predicates without supplying a system from outside them.

Senses.PreferredTarget: the ocean seal shines forth
Senses.Note: The phrase uses the ocean seal as an image of clarity that takes in the many things before it. An inherited scripture line contrasts this radiance with the trouble that arises when thought is grasped; later speakers put the image to different work.

Senses.Explanation: When the ocean seal shines forth, the phrase evokes a wide, clear illumination that takes in the world before it. Xueyan says the light appears when one’s settled assumptions are overturned, then warns that stored sayings alone will not help at death. Zhongfeng places its radiance everywhere in a formal address. Xiaoyin lists daily acts and old cases, refusing to let any become an easy answer to what the light is. Baichi says that after dropping a bellyful of borrowed words and looking for the one who knows, the light appears naturally. Yunwai says that when the listener sees directly, even movement and thought become the ocean seal shining. Liao’an puts the image in a verse of light and openness. Jinian asks whether the image has been shown at a cremation address, then throws down the torch and gives another line.

Entries.SourceTerm: 海底泥牛啣月走，巖前石虎抱兒眠

Senses.PreferredTarget: A mud ox carries the moon beneath the sea; a stone tiger sleeps with its cub before the cliff
SearchAliases: a mud ox carries the moon beneath the sea; a stone tiger sleeps with its cub before the cliff
Senses.Note: Gaofeng’s older four-line stanza begins with a mud ox carrying the moon beneath the sea and a stone tiger sleeping with its cub. Miyun cites it but says the lines still need checking. Tianyin brings the first pair to a memorial for a brother; Feiyin gives the pair as his answer to a question about release from fixed categories. Xueguan cites Gaofeng before challenging what his audience can make of the stanza, and Yichu quotes it before demanding a response. The impossible creatures become a test of what a listener can actually use.

Senses.Explanation: The seas are calm and the rivers clear is a conventional image of settled peace. Sanshan Denglai uses it in a New Year petition for stable rule, Jinul lists it as a name for an undisturbed condition, Baiyu Jingsi pairs it with wind flattening the grass, and Konggu Daocheng answers a question about a peaceful realm with it. Two additional formal statements preserve the political-peace use.

Senses.Explanation: The sea may dry and reveal its bottom, while a person may die without revealing the heart; the fixed warning makes the sea ultimately inspectable but denies the same certainty about a person. Duanqiao Miaolun answers a question about Zhaozhou's dog with the couplet; Liao'an Qingyu uses it after refusing even an articulate account at the monks' gate. Zhenjing Kewen's verse is raised as the line that stopped Duanqiao during his interview with Wuzhun Shifan; Attendant Yu gives the same answer when questioned about the changed cake in the Guanyin saying.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X72/X72n1439.xml). Chan Master Weilin Daopei’s Fragrant Meal Record. Weilin concludes his present hall address for a repentance rite with the paired sky-and-sea line.

Senses.Explanation: The records pair a high sky in which the many forms stand correctly with a broad sea toward which the hundred rivers pay court. Hongjue Min uses the paired line after asking for a word that carries on and circulates the wide gate of the tradition. Mingjue Cong uses it after raising the whisk and asking whose power establishes a peaceful realm. Longyuan Jieqing gives it as the line for repaying imperial favor. Retained public meaning is supported by independent present uses in recorded discourse.

Occurrences.Kwic: 海神知貴不知價。留向人間光照夜。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T47/T47n1997.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuanwu Foguo. Speaker: Yuanwu Keqin in a hall address. A monk asks whether Buddhist teaching remains when rain nourishes everything, then asks how a student should enter when the whole earth is teaching. Yuanwu rejects the monk's proposed agreement and turns to a string of paradoxical images, asking what point they convey. He ends with the sea god who knows a jewel is precious but cannot set its price, leaving its night light among people. The couplet values what the exchange cannot pin down in words.

Occurrences.Kwic: 遂提起云。看看。海神知貴不知價。留與人間光照夜。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T47/T47n1999.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Mi’an. Speaker: Mi'an Xianjie at the raising of a new monastery name plaque. He celebrates the occasion, lifts his staff, and asks the assembly where the decisive move lies before heaven and earth have taken form. He then repeats the sea-god couplet and casts the staff down. The image says the precious thing can be shown and passed among people without being priced by ordinary measures; it serves his immediate public gesture, not an account of a literal jewel sale.

Occurrences.Kwic: 小盡廿九，大盡三十。海神知貴不知價，留與人間光照夜。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X66/X66n1297.xml). Dharma Grove of the Tradition’s Mirror. Voice: an unidentified verse compiler in a sequence of short comments on the Surangama Sutra. After lines on whether sights can be returned to their sources and on the nature beyond names, this verse shifts through calendrical signs and day counts, then says the sea god knows the treasure's value but not its price and leaves it to shine in the human world. The couplet is an inherited poetic image within the compilation, not speech by Ananda or the Buddha.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The headword is an unattributed transmitted verse line in the Grove of the Mirror of the School compilation; no local marker assigns its authorship to the compiler or a named master.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J32/J32nB276.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Buhui Fatong. Speaker: Buhui Fatong in a hall address after quoting the Sutra of Perfect Awakening on not producing or suppressing thoughts. He supplies a verse of ordinary seasons, the fisherman sleeping, and the sea left to its waves; then he throws down his whisk and gives the sea-god couplet. The line turns the scriptural teaching into a present display of a treasure whose worth cannot be fixed by a price. It is Buhui's own closing use of the inherited image.

Senses.Explanation: The sea god recognizes a treasure but cannot assign it a price. Yuanwu uses the image to close a testing hall exchange, and Mi'an uses the couplet while displaying his staff at the hanging of a monastery plaque. An anonymous anthology verse embeds it amid Surangama images, while Buhui gives it as the final line after his own Perfect Awakening verse and whisk gesture.

Senses.PreferredTarget: The sea god knows its worth but cannot price it; left among humans, it shines through the night
AlternateTargets: The sea spirit knows the jewel is precious, not what it costs; it stays in our world and lights the dark
SearchAliases: sea god knows worth not price lights human night
sea spirit jewel shines through night
Senses.Note: The sea god recognizes the jewel's worth but cannot assign a price; left among humans, it lights the night. Buhui, Zhangxue, Hanyu, Yikui, and Xianglin use the full image while pointing or asking an assembly to see what is before them. Baichi answers a question about a teacher's death with it, and Miaoyun applies it to an inherited encounter. The unpriced jewel is valuable precisely in its present light, not as an item a listener can appraise from outside.

Occurrences.Kwic: 火。「大冶飛紅雪，雪寒燄亙天，今朝珍玉別，絕後與光前。」入塔。「團圞無縫，孰能辨主？迅機不動到其中，千眼大悲咸莫睹。」茂修都戎蔣居士起棺。以拄杖扣棺云：「守株待兔，壯夫不為，直透重玄，龍驤虎驟。金烏急，玉兔速，不將姓字挂凌煙，萬里摩雲看俊鶻。」火。「蒼龍不戀沉潭，靈鳳遙天振翮。如是三昧，聖凡罔測，往來三界之賓，出沒為物作則。且道即今以何為驗？全體是金看火色，通身是膽致名標。」子明米頭火。「踏碎虛空，米熟也未？分明足下無私，要顯火光三昧。何謂如此？多虛不如少實。」入塔。「明明不覆藏，要成特地，電捲與星馳，五眼莫能覷。」了悟上座入塔。「歸元有處，不變不遷，拔萃超群，染汙不得。掣電機，看標格，罷卻干戈百艸頭，從教野老稱平貼。」觀音、迦葉、阿難、緣覺、諸天、監齋，諸像開光。師云：「大覺光明，權乘不知；權乘光明，獨覺不知；獨覺光明，聲聞不知；聲聞光明，天人群生之類皆不知也。山僧今日一齊點出，直教光光相羅，如寶絲網。」乃點筆云：「大眾見麼？海神知貴不知價，留與人間光照夜。」古靈禪德火。「皮膚脫落盡，一物鎮長靈。且道是甚麼物？遼天片雪點紅爐。」入塔。「本無位次，豈屬安排？放下便穩，陸地蓮開。」弘宗誓書記起龕。「離我者裏恣汝意，三千里外無非此，臨岐休待涉遲疑，直教俊鷹趁不及。」入塔。「生平烈倔頭，不屑預蟲豸，只知覆卻船，那顧生死海？汝思已矣，我心場哉！今朝功位一時隱，百鳥啣花莫浪猜。」靈旭莊主火。「耕遍祖翁田與地，誰知未熟不臨場？光親證諸三昧，便見優曇遍界香。」明機老禪德火。「人生空百歲，不明此一機。」拈炬云：「會麼？八十翁翁入場屋，真誠不是小兒戲。」卓也巍知藏火。「拶到虛空粉碎，還他卓立不群。劍力上走馬，烈燄裏飛騰，大象不遊於兔徑，從教天下競紛紜。」入塔。「藏身處，欲隱彌露；喚不回，八字打開。坐斷萬機無，團圞無縫卓巍巍。」玉燈昇知藏起龕。「清淨法身濃滴滴，從教扭斷娘生鼻，大鵬纔展翅摩霄，快鷂俊鷹趁不及。」火。「者漢傲頭太煞，癰疽示現多般，不顧刺人心眼，猛火更著油煎。正恁麼時，煎後又作麼生？玉兔東昇燈煥耀，孤光直透斗牛寒。」入塔。「真玉泥中異，泥水也通身，不墮悄然尊貴住，合同船子是通津。」純念碓頭火。「擬心即差，動念即錯，直得純清絕點，猶是真常流注。委悉得麼？火蛇劈面無回互。」映章琛上座封龕。

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 火。「大冶飛紅雪，雪寒燄亙天，今朝珍玉別，絕後與光前。」入塔。「團圞無縫，孰能辨主？迅機不動到其中，千眼大悲咸莫睹。」茂修都戎蔣居士起棺。以拄杖扣棺云：「守株待兔，壯夫不為，直透重玄，龍驤虎驟。金烏急，玉兔速，不將姓字挂凌煙，萬里摩雲看俊鶻。」火。「蒼龍不戀沉潭，靈鳳遙天振翮。如是三昧，聖凡罔測，往來三界之賓，出沒為物作則。且道即今以何為驗？全體是金看火色，通身是膽致名標。」子明米頭火。「踏碎虛空，米熟也未？分明足下無私，要顯火光三昧。何謂如此？多虛不如少實。」入塔。「明明不覆藏，要成特地，電捲與星馳，五眼莫能覷。」了悟上座入塔。「歸元有處，不變不遷，拔萃超群，染汙不得。掣電機，看標格，罷卻干戈百艸頭，從教野老稱平貼。」觀音、迦葉、阿難、緣覺、諸天、監齋，諸像開光。師云：「大覺光明，權乘不知；權乘光明，獨覺不知；獨覺光明，聲聞不知；聲聞光明，天人群生之類皆不知也。山僧今日一齊點出，直教光光相羅，如寶絲網。」乃點筆云：「大眾見麼？海神知貴不知價，留與人間光照夜。」古靈禪德火。「皮膚脫落盡，一物鎮長靈。且道是甚麼物？遼天片雪點紅爐。」入塔。「本無位次，豈屬安排？放下便穩，陸地蓮開。」弘宗誓書記起龕。「離我者裏恣汝意，三千里外無非此，臨岐休待涉遲疑，直教俊鷹趁不及。」入塔。「生平烈倔頭，不屑預蟲豸，只知覆卻船，那顧生死海？汝思已矣，我心場哉！今朝功位一時隱，百鳥啣花莫浪猜。」靈旭莊主火。「耕遍祖翁田與地，誰知未熟不臨場？光親證諸三昧，便見優曇遍界香。」明機老禪德火。「人生空百歲，不明此一機。」拈炬云：「會麼？八十翁翁入場屋，真誠不是小兒戲。」卓也巍知藏火。「拶到虛空粉碎，還他卓立不群。劍力上走馬，烈燄裏飛騰，大象不遊於兔徑，從教天下競紛紜。」入塔。「藏身處，欲隱彌露；喚不回，八字打開。坐斷萬機無，團圞無縫卓巍巍。」玉燈昇知藏起龕。「清淨法身濃滴滴，從教扭斷娘生鼻，大鵬纔展翅摩霄，快鷂俊鷹趁不及。」火。「者漢傲頭太煞，癰疽示現多般，不顧刺人心眼，猛火更著油煎。正恁麼時，煎後又作麼生？玉兔東昇燈煥耀，孤光直透斗牛寒。」入塔。「真玉泥中異，泥水也通身，不墮悄然尊貴住，合同船子是通津。」純念碓頭火。「擬心即差，動念即錯，直得純清絕點，猶是真常流注。委悉得麼？火蛇劈面無回互。」映章琛上座封龕。

Senses.Explanation: The sea is broad enough for fish to leap; the sky is open for birds to fly. An image of unobstructed movement given as an answer or conclusion in current teaching. Current deployments include Yunwai Xingze in J33nB280, Fangrong Ruxi in J29nB249, and Dabo Qian in J40nB472; additional direct uses include Tianan Sheng in J26nB187, Pingyang Min in X66n1297. The full paired image remains the lexical unit. The image marks spacious freedom, not a claim that all actions are equally fitting.

Senses.Explanation: Three teachers use this expansive sea image for a date, a realm, and a staff sermon. At Yun’e Xi’s birthday hall, a monk asks what day it is after offering auspicious images. Yun’e answers with the open sea and the tide of a hundred streams. At Dongshan Pofeng Chong’s hall, a monk asks about a realm of conditioned action and then an unconditioned realm. The teacher answers the latter with the sea image, following his earlier answer about a high sky and ordered forms. At Hefeng’s hall, the teacher strikes his staff twice. He gives the high-sky line at the first strike and the sea-and-streams line at the second, then continues to challenge the assembly. These are separate uses of an image of wide, gathering movement.

Senses.Explanation: To shoulder the responsibility is to take up and sustain the burden of the teaching rather than merely agree with it. Huangbo tells a successor that carrying the great Dharma rests entirely upon him, and Wuyi describes an earlier teacher as having carried that great Dharma at the monastery. Dahui says that anyone resolved to shoulder ‘this matter’ must abandon reliance on clever conceptual calculation. Baichi calls for capable people to join forces in carrying the work of the Chan community, while Meixi contrasts those who shoulder it directly with those who chase reflections and miss it face-to-face. Lianfeng keeps the carrying image visible by asking what, exactly, is being borne on the shoulder. The physical burden supplies the metaphor; the object carried is responsibility for the teaching and its continuation.

Senses.Explanation: The lotus is spent, with no leaves left to hold the rain; the chrysanthemum is battered, yet its branches still defy the frost. An autumn image used as an answer about exhausted forms and remaining vigor. The source-backed uses include Daxiu Zhu in J27nB192, Guxue Zhenzhe in J28nB208, Shengke Deyu in J35nB342, and Baiyu Jingsi in J36nB359. Each is a current use of the full line. The image keeps its paired structure across the records. The first line is from a secular poem by Su Shi; its Chan value comes from four direct applications, not a claim of Zen origin.

Senses.Explanation: The opening line of a four-image verse that pairs the round lotus leaf with a mirror, the pointed water-caltrop with an awl, windblown willow fluff with rolling balls, and rain-struck pear blossoms with flying butterflies. Liangting Jingting uses the expression through direct use of the complete four-image verse followed by a person-and-environment analysis. Baichi Xingyuan independently deploys it through independent recorded-sayings use of the lotus-leaf line. Retained public meaning is supported by independent present uses in recorded discourse.

Senses.Explanation: To guard life, one must kill: the line is paired with 'kill them all, then dwell at ease' in summer-retreat addresses. Zhongfeng sets it among four terse turns; an unnamed questioner asks Wuming where compassion is if the line stands; another unnamed monk uses it to challenge Wanru. Tian'an asks what is killed and explicitly rejects sense objects and entrances, buddhas and ancestors, neither, and both as sufficient answers. Muchen quotes the line in a life-release preface whose following discussion condemns killing animals, so the phrase does not authorize ordinary taking of life.

Senses.Note: Nine J-record settings retain one Xiaoyan poem within distinct present appraisals, not nine original verse authors. Every selected retrospective entry appends a different authored verse or comment, while Fogu turns the couplet into a live rhetorical test. J27 B193 itself is Yinyuan’s retrospective verse treatment, not Xiaoyan’s own surviving work. The interlocutor is locally called Juexue in some recensions and Wuwen in others; both names remain source-named without forcing a roster identity. X80–X85 copied biographies remain reserves.

Occurrences.Kwic: 」師於几上畫個圓相。頌云：南海波斯鼻孔焦，眼空不被舌頭搖，渾身赤骨條條露，險徑相逢接斷橋。第三十二世笑巖寶禪師，參絕學，便問：「十聖三賢已全聖智，如何道不明斯旨？」學厲聲曰：「十聖三賢爾已知，如何是斯旨？速道！」師下語不契。一日，洗菜次，偶一莖菜墮水逐水，圜轉捉不著，忽有省，遂攜籃歸。學見，便問：「是什麼？」師曰：「一籃菜。」學曰：「何不別道一句？」師曰：「請和尚別問來。」後與學圍爐次，學曰：「人人有個本來父母，子之父母今在何處？」師曰：「一火焚之。」學曰：「恁麼則子無父母耶？」師曰：「有即有，佛眼覷不見。」學曰：「子還見麼？」師曰：「某亦不見。」學曰：「為什麼不見？」師曰：「若見，則非真父母。」遂呈偈曰：「本來真父母，歷劫不曾離。起坐承他力，寒溫亦共知。相逢不相見，相見不相識。為問今何在？分明舉似師。」學深肯之。頌云：中流勘破較些些，那更拈提舉似爺？覿面風光猶自可，到頭霜月落誰家？第三十三世幻有傳禪師，聞燈花爆聲有省，直造北方，參笑巖求證。巖曰：「汝將從前得力處一一說來。」師具實荅語中間，巖驀趯出鞋曰：「向者裏道一句看。」遂把師話端一齊打斷。師通夕不寐，明晨佇立簷下。巖見喚師，師回顧，巖翹一足，作修羅障日月勢，師當下脫然。一日，巖入堂曰：「我者拄杖要與人，有要底麼？」首座曰：「某甲要。」巖曰：「汝要作麼？」座曰：「要他鏟斷天下人舌根。」巖以杖架肩曰：「楖栗橫擔不顧人，直入千峰萬峰去。」師躍然下禪床曰：「恁麼須分付某甲往前迎取。」巖笑曰：「汝當久久執持一番，始可打草去也。」乃贈一笠
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J27/J27nB193.xml). Yinyuan Longqi retells Xiaoyan's questioning by source-named Juexue: the true parents are burned in one fire yet exist beyond even a Buddha's sight. Xiaoyan presents the full poem including the selected couplet, and his teacher approves. Yinyuan's new following verse asks why the matter is still brought before the father and whose house receives the final frosty moon. This is a retrospective appraisal of the poem's presentation, with Xiaoyan retained as its quoted author.

After the full poem and approval, her own verse returns to the leaf turning in the stream, the shock through the body and half a verse sustaining the ancestral transmission, ending with one lamp igniting many. It is a distinct current poem following a shared old case, not another original declaration about the parents.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J33/J33nB281.xml). Zizhou Chuan retells the Wuwen recension and then explicitly criticizes Xiaoyan as carrying a bottomless basket that still bears a load; before Zizhou's own shout even fire would have difficulty burning it. His new verse says that the basket-bearing encounter had never been separate, yet the face-to-face presentation was allowed through, and returns to burning the parents and repaying their kindness through ash and smoke. This directly tests the old poem's asserted intimacy rather than merely copying its words.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J38/J38nB427.xml). Zhulang Chesheng quotes Xiaoyan's poem under the Wuwen recension, follows it with the comment about adornment through concentration and wisdom across inconceivable aeons, then composes a new verse on responsive warmth and care. It explicitly names the true parents across vast aeons and their whole body appearing throughout the worlds. The new verse engages the selected couplet's inseparable supporting and shared knowing, rather than serving as an unrelated entry decoration.

Zizhou Chuan retells the Wuwen recension and then explicitly criticizes Xiaoyan as carrying a bottomless basket that still bears a load; before Zizhou's own shout even fire would have difficulty burning it. Senses.Explanation: In Xiaoyan's verse, the true original parents have never been separate from him: their power supports rising and sitting, and cold and warmth are known together. Yet he says that meeting is not seeing and seeing is not recognizing. Later teachers examine how this intimate dependence can be shown, or reject the couplet as a ready-made explanation of the indestructible body. Yinyuan Longqi retells Xiaoyan's questioning by source-named Juexue: the true parents are burned in one fire yet exist beyond even a Buddha's sight. Xiaoyan presents the full poem including the selected couplet, and his teacher approves. Yinyuan's new following verse asks why the matter is still brought before the father and whose house receives the final frosty moon. This is a retrospective appraisal of the poem's presentation, with Xiaoyan retained as its quoted author. Qiyuan Xinggang carries the Juexue version of the vegetable-washing and parents encounter. After the full poem and approval, her own verse returns to the leaf turning in the stream, the shock through the body and half a verse sustaining the ancestral transmission, ending with one lamp igniting many. The verse connects Xiaoyan's account of inseparable support with its recognition and succession. It is a distinct current poem following a shared old case, not another original declaration about the parents. Jizong Che's recension calls Xiaoyan's interlocutor Wuwen and ends the old exchange with explicit permission to inherit the tradition. Her new verse follows the leaf drifting downstream, the many-armed asura unable to hold it, and the return to the hall with the basket raised. These images appraise the presentation of the realization that the full parents poem states. Jizong does not become the speaker of Xiaoyan's selected couplet merely by versifying the encounter. Zizhou Chuan retells the Wuwen recension and then explicitly criticizes Xiaoyan as carrying a bottomless basket that still bears a load; before Zizhou's own shout even fire would have difficulty burning it. His new verse says that the basket-bearing encounter had never been separate, yet the face-to-face presentation was allowed through, and returns to burning the parents and repaying their kindness through ash and smoke. This directly tests the old poem's asserted intimacy rather than merely copying its words. At Liu's mother's birthday sermon, Fogu Xingwen raises the whisk and asks what the diamond-indestructible body is. He offers several possible accounts, including being master of appearances, the selected rising-and-sitting couplet, a voice without visible form and light beyond sun and moon. He rejects such calculations as scooping the sea with a shell or viewing the sky through a tube, then speaks of meeting forms according to the person to be helped. The old poetic line is an explicit candidate answer put under pressure in this live event. Dafang Xinghai retells the Juexue version of Xiaoyan's parents poem, then gives his own verse: a complete pouring-out at the rapids, grasping empty sky to present to the teacher, bare hands without another plan and a thief turning in an empty room. The fresh images appraise what it means to offer the apparently intimate realization without a possessed object. A local repeated speaker marker in the old dialogue is preserved in the Chinese rather than silently repaired. He also calls the teacher's kindly request for another sentence nectar turned into poison and supplies his own alternative, that the arrow departed long ago. His verse returns to chasing vegetable fragments downstream and carrying household provisions into the street. This is an unmistakably separate critical use of the inherited poem. Occurrences.Kwic: 慶快之日，離得生死過患邪？又如人歸家相似，你若到家了，自見家裏種種物件，非涂中疑似竟界也。學道人見得親人處真實，即目前種種酬應都是受用了者事。且如何是分歲底一句？坐到四更後，寒與煖分開。」小參。「孫賓今日開鋪，更無一人垂顧，可憐三尺龍須，喚作尋常破布。山僧今日也有箇程式。」以拂子豎起，复揮數下，云：「以此振鈴申召請，了無一箇向前來，不如室裏喫茶去。」良久，云：「此句待明日續。」便歸方丈。小參。「南泉因甘贄行者打破屋裏𩰫子，是分典座缽中食，療飯頭肚裏饑；雲門叫雪峰和尚卸卻項上鐵枷，是解猛虎頸上鈴，換驪龍頷下珠。先德固是拈提向上宗乘，一往觀來未是好手，不見才起摸畫樣便落今時，怎如山僧者裏隨流任性取快適時？寒則圍盧箸挑松火，倦則高眠震地齁鼾，饑則嚼菜根，渴則飲清流，佛亦不管、祖亦不顧，了無閒論，豈有可為？」良久，拈拄杖，云：「既如此，又何必開兩片皮作甚麼？大眾！不因桃李春，那得行谿上？」解制，小參。「從來無箇踦絆，無耑畫地為牢，坐了一百餘日，箇箇體癈形消，通身筋骨炙爛。究竟何有一豪？兄弟！身世不有，人法兩忘，又作麼生？前三三，後三三，藍水遠從千澗落，玉山高并兩峰寒。」袁江毛提舉請小參。泰書記問：「升堂請益即不問，雲風清意如何？」師云：「風飄素景寒。」泰云：「月照關河靜，鐙明方丈清。」師云：「才向峰頭立，急雨過關西。」

Senses.Explanation: Hongzhi closes a verse on Luoshan and Yantou’s exchange with a question about arising and ceasing. Luoshan asks Yantou what to do while arising and ceasing never stop; Yantou presses him to identify who arises and ceases. Hongzhi’s verse answers the old encounter through images of cut vines, a leopard changing its markings, and a dragon riding thunder before it asks what the turmoil is. Hongzhi’s own record gives the verse, a Chan anthology transmits it, and Tianqi annotates the same verse in a separate treatment.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J28/J28nB208.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Guxue Zhenzhe: At the Huangbo invitation sermon, an unnamed monk presses Guxue on whether he is going or staying. Guxue first answers with an image of a fishing rod, then gives this farewell couplet after the monk's congratulatory reply. It places departure from home inside the live question of his move to Huangbo; Guxue is the current speaker, and the monk supplies the prompts. His ensuing verse about returning an old friend to his homeland develops the same departure and return imagery.

Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuejian: Yuejian addresses the assembly after picturing a traveler who has come three thousand miles, worn out seven sitting mats, and still chases clever formulations without reaching the matter. Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chushi Fanqi: In an assembly talk Chushi compares the great matter both before and after it is clear to mourning one's parents, then asks the listeners whether attainment changes that situation. He answers his own question with the farewell couplet: seeing off another person recalls one's own leaving home. It brings the contrast back to an immediate human scene, without attributing the line to the monk in the following separate exchange. Chushi is the present utterer.

Senses.Explanation: The farewell couplet turns seeing another person off into a recollection of one's own departure from home. Guxue answers the questioner's inquiry about going to Huangbo; Wuchu comments on Xuedou's encounter with an attendant; Heshan answers a guest-host question; Yuejian shifts a warning about stale practice; Chushi answers his own question about the great matter. These are five different present deployments of the same image, with Heshan's useful lamp interview retained as a distinct witness.

Occurrences.Kwic: 起小陽春。乃以拂子空中一點，曰：還見麼？還聞麼？若道見，作麼生見？若道聞，作麼生聞？於此兩楹之間，云何剖露？要會麼？滿眼覰不見，滿耳聽不聞，一堂風冷淡，千古意分明。上堂。秋風秋雨頗相宜，萬水千山木葉飛。堪笑靈雲回首處，何須花發始忘機。何故？諸禪德，秋風蕭索，秋山葉落，秋雨霖漓，秋天寥廓。祖師心印全彰，靈雲鼻孔穿却。分明一道恩光，曠劫無形寂寞。五湖衲子急歸來，休向途中亂穿鑿。莫穿鑿，體用從來非自他，作者不求無病藥。擊禪牀。因事上堂，僧問：長安夜夜家家月，幾處笙歌幾處愁？師曰：總是闍棃分上事。僧云：和尚也不要疑著。師曰：一言已出，駟馬難追。師乃曰：事久多變，信知有矣。何故？雪後始知松柏操，事難方見丈夫心。諸禪德還委悉麼？設使智過鶖子、辯若滿慈，到這裏無你開口處、無你議論處。既然恁麼，畢竟如何？要會麼？大樹大皮裹，小樹小皮纏。上堂。金烏當午，文彩全彰；玉兔沈輝，影像俱寂。通同實際，一體無諸；不落今時，識情罔測。混融凡聖，佛眼難窺。所以道：髑髏常干世界，鼻孔摩觸家風。本色衲僧，云何辨白？瞥然契悟，大事圓明

Senses.Explanation: Chang’an’s great road is the broad, direct road to the capital. The records place it among monastery approaches, in case-verses, and in direct questions about where the road is met. Yangshan Qingjian says the pines lining the way go straight through to Chang’an’s road. Dawei Fabao’s Bodhidharma verse calls it straight as a string; Miyin Zhenchuan answers that one steps on it upon leaving the gate; Panshan Langkong Shun calls it level and open.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J40/J40nB494.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Yushan. A monk asks Yushan Shangsi why one would leave after rolling up the mat; Yushan replies with the Chang’an warning and continues answering the monk’s next questions.

Senses.Explanation: Three teachers use the old Chang’an warning to answer a lay visitor, caution a retreatant, and challenge a monk in a hall. Layman Shen raises his fist to Yichu Wuyuan and asks why the ancients would not settle at this point; Yichu answers with the Chang’an warning. Yingning Zhijing later warns an aspirant that even effortless eating and sleeping can become a comfortable resting place; he cites the old line, strikes his staff, and adds a military image about refusing to sit in a peace one has won. In Yushan Shangsi’s separate hall, a monk asks why one would roll up the mat and leave after a household collapse; Yushan uses the same line as his answer, then responds to further questions. The shared old saying supports three different live exchanges.

AlternateTargets: Chang'an may bustle, but my country is settled

Senses.Note: In the earlier Yaoshan exchange, Gao the novice answers a question about busy Chang'an with this pair. Daxiu later gives it when asked about the world consumed by fire; Baichi speaks it in a present sermon and adds the image of sleeping warmly; Jingting uses it to answer his own question about ease beyond things. The two realms name a contrast within the encounter rather than a literal pair of states.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X66/X66n1296.xml). Compilation of the School Gate’s “Raising Old Cases”. Muyun Tongmen comments on Deshan and Linji’s old meeting, asks the assembly whether they can distinguish it, strikes the Chan bench, and voices the Chang’an line himself.

Senses.Explanation: Three teachers use the Chang’an line to press listeners toward direct seeing in two halls and one case comment. Feiyin Tongrong argues in a hall that even ordinary people can stand above entangling categories; he introduces the Chang’an line with “therefore it is said,” then shoulders his staff and leaves. Meixi Fudu tells another assembly that teaching is visible everywhere without waiting for his own words, looks around, and closes with the line before striking his staff. In an anthology of old cases, Muyun Tongmen comments on Deshan and Linji, asks the assembly whether they can distinguish the encounter, strikes the Chan bench, and gives the same line. The inherited phrase is used as a live challenge in three separate settings; it is not voiced by Deshan or Linji in the anthology.

Entries.SourceTerm: 長安風月貫今昔，那箇男兒摸壁行

Senses.PreferredTarget: Chang’an’s wind and moon span past and present; what true man would grope along a wall?
SearchAliases: Chang’an’s wind and moon span past and present; what true man would grope along a wall?
Senses.Note: Four distinct current sermons retain four exact speakers. Hanxiu Ruqian, Yuan’an Benfeng, Yikui Yuankui and Liaotang Weiyi each voice the couplet themselves; quoted Buddhas and old teachers in their introductions are not substituted as its utterer. B386 is source-proved Benfeng, and B388 explicitly identifies Yuankui rather than the other roster master called Yikui. The recurring wording does not make these different occasions one copied sermon.

At the winter-retreat closing small assembly, Hanxiu Ruqian contrasts a tightly secured barrier with an opened bag that allows free movement. The monk can stay or travel without a trace or attachment, always on the road while never leaving home. Hanxiu says he has directly displayed the matter in every direction and asks whether the audience knows, closing with the headword. The open capital landscape answers the possibility of still groping after a path when going and staying have already been released.

Yuan'an Benfeng follows questions about precepts, Nanquan's cat, Deshan and Danxia by saying that precept, concentration and wisdom cannot be fixed in their names. He warns that grasping names resembles marking a boat to find a fallen sword or waiting at a stump for rabbits. He asks what finally follows and gives the couplet as the close of this critique of borrowed markers.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J37/J37nB388.xml). In a whisk talk, Yikui Yuankui revisits the abbot's seven questions and promise to give the bowl-bag whether answers fit or fail. He rejects the brothers' interpretations as mixed nectar and poison, confusion or concealed stinginess, saying they have missed the teacher's point. He then brings the bowl-bag before them himself, asks who can accept it directly, throws down the staff and gives the headword. The couplet closes a present act of offering, not a quotation assigned to the abbot whose questions prompted it.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X71/X71n1417.xml). At the Buddha-awakening hall talk, Liaotang Weiyi briefly recounts leaving the city, cutting the hair, six years of hardship and awakening on seeing the morning star. He interrupts that familiar sequence with an exclamation and gives the couplet. The wind and moon across past and present turn the commemorated event toward the assembly's present capacity to see. Liaotang speaks the conclusion; the Buddha is the figure whose story he has just raised, not its grammatical utterer.

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 坐九年空著忙，西歸隻履好慚惶。報恩一句無人會，徒仰聲光遍八荒。上堂：識心達本，故號沙門。當知山河大地、日月星辰、人畜草木種種物象從何發現？終日行住坐臥、喜怒哀樂種種施為承誰恩力？良久：只知開口易，不覺舌頭長。冬至，上堂。逢來一夏又一夏，過了一冬還一冬。身世難將金石固，頭顱易見雪霜蒙。泥牛夜吼滄江月，鐵󳬧晨飛碧嶂風。四七二三諸宿德，曾無一法可流通。上堂，舉：教中道：燈能顯色，如是見者，是眼非燈；眼能見色，如是知者，是心非眼。師云：釋迦老子抑下威光，曲垂方便，也只道得一半。便下座。淵西堂至，上堂：倒却門前剎竿著，兄呼弟應久無聞，住山鈯斧輕拋下，喜見西丘嫡骨孫。佛成道，上堂：逾城出家，拔劒斬髮。雪山六載，麻麥充飢。夜覩明星，成無上覺。嗄！長安風月貫今昔，那箇男兒摸壁行？藏主、維那至，上堂。顯藏主對李殿院側身而立，水到渠成。克賓維那法戰不勝，棒了罰錢，雲開月現。以拂子畫一畫：石牛闌古路，一馬生三寅。除夜，小參。似地擎山，不知山之孤峻；如石含玉，不知玉之無瑕。不可以智知，不可以識識，不可以語言造，不可以寂默通。一年三百六十日，諸人每日穿僧堂、入佛殿，拈香擇火，渴飲飢飡，或語、或默，或喜、或嗔，種種施為，何嘗欠少？逗到歲盡年窮，聞鼓聲上法堂，鴈行而立，圖箇什麼？山僧據曲彔木床，說黃道黑，指東畫西，也是𦘕蛇添足。驀拈主丈卓一下：葫蘆棚上掛冬瓜，黃檗樹頭懸蜜果。復舉：六祖大師示眾云：吾有一物，無頭、無尾，無名、無字，無背、無面，諸人還識麼？時，荷澤神會出云：是諸佛之本源，乃神會之佛性。祖乃打一棒，云：我喚

Senses.Explanation: The wind and moon of the capital are openly present across time; the closing question asks why anyone should still feel blindly for a way. Different teachers use the couplet after freeing travel and residence, exposing attachment to teaching labels, offering the begging bowl directly, or recounting the Buddha's awakening. The rebuke concerns the hearer's present hesitation, not directions to a physical wall in Chang'an. At the winter-retreat closing small assembly, Hanxiu Ruqian contrasts a tightly secured barrier with an opened bag that allows free movement. The monk can stay or travel without a trace or attachment, always on the road while never leaving home. Hanxiu says he has directly displayed the matter in every direction and asks whether the audience knows, closing with the headword. The open capital landscape answers the possibility of still groping after a path when going and staying have already been released. Yuan'an Benfeng follows questions about precepts, Nanquan's cat, Deshan and Danxia by saying that precept, concentration and wisdom cannot be fixed in their names. He warns that grasping names resembles marking a boat to find a fallen sword or waiting at a stump for rabbits. Even old awakening stories can put water in ears and sand in eyes, sending descendants away from what is present. He asks what finally follows and gives the couplet as the close of this critique of borrowed markers. He rejects the brothers' interpretations as mixed nectar and poison, confusion or concealed stinginess, saying they have missed the teacher's point. He then brings the bowl-bag before them himself, asks who can accept it directly, throws down the staff and gives the headword. The couplet closes a present act of offering, not a quotation assigned to the abbot whose questions prompted it. He interrupts that familiar sequence with an exclamation and gives the couplet. The wind and moon across past and present turn the commemorated event toward the assembly's present capacity to see. Liaotang speaks the conclusion; the Buddha is the figure whose story he has just raised, not its grammatical utterer.

Entries.SourceTerm: 長將日月為天眼，指出須彌作壽山

Senses.PreferredTarget: Make sun and moon the eyes of heaven; point to Mount Sumeru as a mountain of long life
AlternateTargets: Take the sun and moon as heaven’s eyes, and Mount Sumeru as a mountain of longevity
SearchAliases: sun and moon heaven eyes Mount Sumeru longevity
Mount Sumeru mountain of long life
Senses.Note: The local challenge and the current teacher's response govern the reading; quoted evaluations are not universal factual claims.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：「日照千山翠，春回萬木新，今日和尚誕辰，畢竟呈何祥瑞？」師云：「有星皆拱北。」進云：「祇如祝誕一句又作麼生？」師云：「無水不朝東。」進云：「長將日月為天眼，指出須彌作壽山。」師不顧，乃云：
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J36/J36nB345.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zhuyan Yan of Suzhou. The cosmic eyes and mountain of longevity form a blessing image, but each occasion tests how it is used. At Zhu'an Zhenyan's fiftieth birthday, an unnamed monk asks about auspicious signs and birthday words, receives stars turning north and waters flowing east, then offers the headword. Zhu'an pays it no attention and begins an address in which neither before nor after one's parents' birth is there a fixed teaching to say, amid street firecrackers, drums and boundless lamps. The line is the monk's ceremonial offering, not the teacher's assertion that he has acquired an immortal body.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: 進云 introduces the exact line after the monk’s question; 師不顧 marks Zhu’an’s separate response and no personal name is supplied.

Occurrences.Kwic: 聖節，上堂。「大哉乾元，萬物資始，鈞陶有象，垂拱無為，是謂天中之天、聖中之聖。且道全身奉重如何舉揚？」豎拂子，云：「長將日月為天眼，指出須彌作壽山。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J37/J37nB392.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Hansong Cao. At an imperial celebration, Hansong Zhicao invokes the creative beginning of heaven, the source of living things and rule through effortless composure. He asks how complete reverence should be brought forth, raises his whisk and gives the pair. Here he voices the blessing himself as an answer to the ritual demand. Sun, moon and Mount Sumeru give it comprehensive scale; the source does not turn them into medical guarantees of the ruler's actual lifespan.

Occurrences.Kwic: 士問：「今日敦請和尚登座舉揚箇事，和尚如何相為？」師云：「長將日月為天眼，指出須彌作壽山。」進云：「世尊睹星大悟，請問在睹星邊？不在睹星邊？」師云：「那裏得者消息來？」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J38/J38nB408.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Aziwa of Haichuang. At an awakening-day discourse, a layman asks Azi Jinwu how he will respond to the invitation to expound the matter. Azi answers with the blessing pair. The layman then asks whether the Buddha's awakening lies in seeing the star or apart from it, and Azi challenges where he obtained that information; an attempt to escape both alternatives is called an old vine entangling monks and laity. The grand image opens a continuing test of the questioner, not a final proof that the occasion has already been understood.

Occurrences.Kwic: 陞座，祝聖罷，乃云：大道只在目前，要且目前難覩，欲識大道真體，不離聲色言語。拂子，擊禪牀，云：這箇是聲。豎拂子，云：這箇是色。喚什麼作大道？長將日月為天眼，指出須彌作壽山。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X69/X69n1355.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Wumen Huikai. After the ruler's blessing at an assembly, Wumen Huikai says the great way is directly present yet hard to see, and cannot be separated from sound, visible form and language. He strikes the seat with the whisk and calls that sound, raises the whisk and calls that form, then asks what one calls the way and gives the pair. The actual gesture and question bring the ceremonial imagery into present recognition. The pair does not instruct the assembly to search for literal giant eyes in the sky.

Entries.SourceTerm: 長憶江南三月裏、鷓鴣啼處百花香
Entries.CreatedBy: Codex Lane C C141-145 full-case construction

Senses.PreferredTarget: I long remember Jiangnan in the third month, where amid partridge cries all the flowers are fragrant
SearchAliases: partridges call where all flowers are fragrant
Senses.Note: The spring scene works as an answer within each exchange; its role depends on the question and the present speaker. Xueyan’s quotation of Fengxue and his later reuse belong to one inherited couplet family.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問風穴：語默涉離微，如何通不犯？風穴云：長憶江南三月裏，鷓鴣啼處百花香。風穴老漢與麼道，是則得路便行、到手便用，依舊未出得語默離微在。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X70/X70n1397.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Xueyan Zuqin (雪巖祖欽禪師語錄). Quoted speaker of this occurrence: Fengxue Yanzhao; current raiser and critic: Xueyan Zuqin. In a hall address Xueyan raises an old monk’s question about passing through speech and silence without offending either. Fengxue answers with remembering Jiangnan in spring, when partridges call among fragrant flowers. Xueyan says the old answer was readily available but still did not escape the speech-and-silence problem; later in the same address he repeats the couplet as his own test. This row records Fengxue’s quoted answer and Xueyan’s immediate criticism.
Occurrences.VariantForm: 長憶江南三月裏，鷓鴣啼處百花香

Occurrences.Kwic: 前百丈、後百丈，未審還有優劣也無？師云：長憶江南三月裏，鷓鴣啼處百花香。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X85/X85n1592.xml). The Hidden Black Beans Collection (揞黑豆集). Speaker: Ruoan Tongwen, identified by the governing 杭州南㵎理安箬菴問禪師 heading. In a sequence of questions about the old Baizhang and the later Baizhang, the questioner asks whether one is better than the other. Ruoan answers with the Jiangnan spring couplet, declining to rank them in the terms offered. The next lines turn to a separate account of Ruoan’s final travels, so the quote is confined to this exchange.
Occurrences.VariantForm: 長憶江南三月裏，鷓鴣啼處百花香

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂：有句無句，如藤倚樹。樹倒藤枯，句歸何處？良久，曰：長憶江南三月裏，鷓鴣啼處百花香。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X84/X84n1579.xml). Continuation of the Record Pointing at the Moon (續指月錄). Speaker: Kuchan Zijing (枯禪自鏡), identified by the raw 慶元天童枯禪自鏡禪師 section heading at 0040c18; he is not linked to the lineage roster. In a hall address Kuchan raises the saying that a phrase and no phrase are like a vine clinging to a tree, then asks where the phrase goes when the tree falls and vine withers. After a pause he answers with the remembered Jiangnan spring and calling partridges. This is a new deployment of the inherited couplet in Kuchan’s own question, not Po’an Zuxian’s voice.
Occurrences.VariantForm: 長憶江南三月裏，鷓鴣啼處百花香

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: Kuchan Zijing (枯禪自鏡) is the speaker named in the raw X84 cb:div/head at 0040c18 as 慶元天童枯禪自鏡禪師. The following 上堂 at 0040c20–21 contains the exact answer and remains inside his section.

Occurrences.Kwic: 乃云：「未達境唯心，起種種分別；達境唯心已，分別即不生。」良久，卓拄杖一下云：「長憶江南三月裏，鷓鴣啼處百花香。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J36/J36nB355.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Hengxiulin of Lülüo (綠蘿恒秀林禪師語錄). Speaker: Hengxiulin Falin in a hall address requested by a lay patron and other devotees. After a monk’s questions about a lotus before and after emerging from water, Hengxiulin says that when one understands that objects are mind, discriminating thought no longer arises. He pauses, strikes his staff, and gives the Jiangnan spring couplet. The image closes his exchange as a sensory answer after his teaching on discrimination, rather than continuing the preceding Xueyan debate.
Occurrences.VariantForm: 長憶江南三月裏，鷓鴣啼處百花香

Senses.Explanation: The remembered Jiangnan spring is a poetic answer to questions that resist a ranking or conceptual formula. Fengxue Yanzhao first uses the couplet to answer how to pass through speech and silence; Xueyan Zuqin quotes it, criticizes Fengxue’s handling, and later repeats the same lines as a test. Ruoan Tongwen offers it when asked to rank two Baizhang figures. Kuchan Zijing uses it after asking where a phrase goes when the tree supporting its vine falls, and Hengxiulin Falin gives it after a staff strike in a discussion of discrimination. These later speakers reuse the inherited image in different local encounters. The X84 speaker is Kuchan, as its source heading shows, rather than the published Po’an attribution.

Senses.PreferredTarget: senior elder
Senses.Note: An honorific for a senior monk or teacher. It can serve as direct address, identify a specific elder by name, describe a newly installed abbot, or refer to a group of monastic leaders. The title alone does not identify who is speaking.

Occurrences.Kwic: 嚴付授第十三No.1259禪門鍛鍊說江西南康雲居山真如禪寺晦山戒顯著堅誓忍苦第一堅誓忍苦第一夫為長老者，據佛祖之正位，則應紹佛祖之家業；作人天之師範，則應開人天之眼目。人天眼目者何？佛性是已。佛祖
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X63/X63n1259.xml). Discourse on Training in the Chan Gate (禪門鍛鍊說). At the opening of his Discourse on Training in the Chan Gate, Huishan Jiexian says that a person serving as elder occupies the place of buddhas and ancestors, must continue their work, and should open the eyes of people and heavenly beings. The term names a teaching office with obligations, not mere age.

Occurrences.Kwic: 新長老又排場，嫩綠駸駸過短牆。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB187.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Tian’an Sheng (天岸昇禪師語錄). On first taking charge of Dajue monastery, Tian’an Sheng offers a verse before the ancestral hall and calls himself the new elder who has again taken up the occasion. The honorific names the newly installed teacher in his own opening rite, rather than a separate narrator’s label.

Occurrences.Kwic: 雪山有五百仙人。覩茲瑞應。飛空而至。禮尊者足。胡跪白言。我於長老。當證佛法。願垂大慈。度脫我等。尊者默然受請

Senses.Explanation: The title 長老 marks a senior monastic teacher. Huishan Jiexian defines the elder’s office as inheriting the work of buddhas and ancestors and guiding others. Tian’an Sheng calls himself the new elder during his installation at Dajue. A novice who later became Emperor Dazhong respectfully calls Huangbo elder while questioning his bow before the Buddha. Fayan Wenyi addresses Baozi Elder in a question about penetrating light. Layman Zeng Hui refers to Qing Elder while speaking with Xuedou about Zhaozhou’s old-woman case. Five hundred immortals address Ananda as elder when seeking instruction. A separate outline record narrates the court’s summons to Fori Yue and six Chan elders. These scenes show an office or respectful standing, with different speakers and referents.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Elder, there is a guest in your room; you had better return.
SearchAliases: Elder, there is a guest in your room; you had better return.
Senses.Note: Four current J verse settings appraise one inherited Baizhang reply. Baizhang Weizheng is the headword speaker, and the elder is his questioner and addressee; Miyun, Tian’an, Dabian and Luyan supply different present verses. The J39 verse is also reproduced in X66, so X66 adds no independent family. Their match does not by itself prove a direction of borrowing or a first author. X80/X81 parallel biographies remain reserves.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J10/J10nA158.xml). Miyun Yuanwu quotes the elder seeing sunlight through the window and asking whether the window approaches the sun or the sun the window. Baizhang answers with the guest and return. Miyun's own verse repeats the alternatives, says one recognizes either the object or the light, and reads the reply as waking the elder face to face without another matter. It ends with immediate release and returning to the room. This is a distinct interpretive verse, not an added explanation spoken by Baizhang.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB187.xml). Tian'an Sheng quotes the same question in the reverse order and Baizhang's reply, then gives a darker present appraisal. The guest digs the earth to seek the sky while the host lengthens a duck's legs and shortens a crane's; sunset, mournful wind and a lonely mountain window follow. His verse questions both sides' handling rather than simply celebrating homecoming. The headword remains Baizhang's old response inside Tian'an's different poem.

Occurrences.Kwic: 吞盡大千界，萬象光含無表裏，迷頭認影不相當，對面白雲千萬里。南泉山下有一菴主，人謂曰：「近日南泉和尚出世，何不去禮見？」主曰：「非但南泉出世，直饒千佛出興，我亦不去。」師聞，乃令趙州去勘。州去便設拜，主不顧。州從東過西，又從西過東，主亦不顧。州曰：「艸賊大敗。」遂拽下簾子，便歸舉似，師曰：「我從來疑著者漢。」次日，與沙彌攜茶一缾、盞三隻到菴，擲向地上，乃曰：「昨日底！昨日底！」主曰：「昨日底是甚麼？」師於沙彌背上拍一下，曰：「賺我來！賺我來！」拂袖便回。好箇擔板漢，橫身一條銕，智勇李將軍，兩度拗不折。出師重決龍蛇陣，當鋒連下頂門楔，馬陵道下死龐涓，千古英雄常淚血。百丈惟政禪師。有老宿見日影透窗，問師：「為復窗就日？日就窗？」師曰：「長老房中有客，歸去好。」問來隱密，畣不囊藏，運籌帷幄，捉賊擒王。驀喚一聲歸去好，和雲帶露溼秋光。酈村自滿禪師上堂：「古今不異，法爾如然，更復何也？雖然如此，者箇事大有人罔措在。」僧問：「不落古今，請師直道。」師曰：「情知爾罔措。」僧欲進語，師曰：「將謂老僧落伊古今。」曰：「如何即是？」師曰：「魚騰碧漢，階級難飛。」曰：「如何免得此過？」師曰：「若是龍形，誰論高下？」僧禮拜，師曰：「苦哉！屈哉！誰人似我？」迥絕威音與目前，古今不落本天然，擬求直道翻成曲，蚤隔程途萬八千。欲免過，轉堪憐，天上人間誰似我？驅雷掣電鼓風煙。南源道明禪師上堂：「快馬一鞭，至人一言。有事何不出頭來？無事各自珍重！」僧問：「一言作麼生？」師乃吐舌云：「待我有廣長舌相，即向汝道。」一言
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J29/J29nB248.xml). Dabian Xianquan raises the window-and-sun question and the guest reply, then calls the question hidden and the answer unconcealing. His own verse turns to planning within the command tent and capturing thief and king, before the sudden call to go back carries cloud and dew through autumn light. The guest and return thus become an appraisal of responsive strategy. Dabian is the new verse author, while Baizhang remains the speaker who sends the elder away.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J39/J39nB452.xml). Luyan He appends a verse to the inherited dialogue that repeats sun and window, says unresolved preceding objects waste discussion, and asks the guest to return until reaching the place where there is no return. The exact verse also appears in the X66 compilation. This entry retains Luyan's recorded current use once and discloses the match, rather than claiming the compilation supplies another independent interpretation or proving who borrowed from whom.

Senses.Explanation: Baizhang redirects an elder's question about sunlight and a window toward the guest in his own room. Later verses hear this as a call to return, criticize both guest and host, or recast it as strategic handling. The invitation home interrupts an abstract choice about which thing approaches the other; it does not answer that choice on its own terms. Miyun Yuanwu quotes the elder seeing sunlight through the window and asking whether the window approaches the sun or the sun the window. Baizhang answers with the guest and return. Miyun's own verse repeats the alternatives, says one recognizes either the object or the light, and reads the reply as waking the elder face to face without another matter. It ends with immediate release and returning to the room. This is a distinct interpretive verse, not an added explanation spoken by Baizhang. Tian'an Sheng quotes the same question in the reverse order and Baizhang's reply, then gives a darker present appraisal. The guest digs the earth to seek the sky while the host lengthens a duck's legs and shortens a crane's; sunset, mournful wind and a lonely mountain window follow. His verse questions both sides' handling rather than simply celebrating homecoming. The headword remains Baizhang's old response inside Tian'an's different poem. Dabian Xianquan raises the window-and-sun question and the guest reply, then calls the question hidden and the answer unconcealing. His own verse turns to planning within the command tent and capturing thief and king, before the sudden call to go back carries cloud and dew through autumn light. The guest and return thus become an appraisal of responsive strategy. Dabian is the new verse author, while Baizhang remains the speaker who sends the elder away. Senses.Explanation: Nanquan lifts Huangbo's hat at their parting and contrasts its smallness with his vast body. Huangbo says the whole world is within it; Nanquan asks where that leaves him, and Huangbo puts on the hat and goes. The later verses read the sequence through mutual giving and taking, host and guest, and a scale not measured by ordinary dimensions. ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 用而不知。畢竟不知箇什麼？包羲曾未動，爻象已分明。歲節，小參。雪峰納欵於鰲山店上，是得德山力耶？得巖頭力。臨濟𡎺拳於高安灘頭，是得黃蘗力耶？得大愚力。你這一隊師僧，尋常三三兩兩，口赫赤地，談論佛法，明辨古今，到者裏還明辨得出麼？古人則且置，山僧與主丈子為師友之交，一年之間，東拄西撑，左提右挈，扶過斷橋水，伴歸無月村，爾我相資，彼此得力。如今﨟月三十日也，且道者許多得力處，閻羅老子面前還使得著麼？若道使得著，坐殺諸人；若道使不著，走殺諸人。不如主丈自主丈，山僧自山僧，庭空積深雪，池冷起氷稜，樓上未吹新歲角，窻前且點舊年燈，唵齒臨部臨吽吽。舉：漸源一日因雲盖和尚至，卷起簾，方丈內坐。雲盖來見，遂下却簾，便歸客位。漸源令侍者下去，傳語云：長老遠來不易，猶隔津在。雲盖擒住侍者，與一掌。者云：未得打某甲，有堂頭和尚在。雲盖云：只為有堂頭和尚，所以打你。者回，舉似漸源。源云：猶隔津在。師拈云：探驪頷，抉驪珠，還他作者；據虎頭，収虎尾，須是其人。雖然，總被侍者勘破。結夏，小參。護生須是殺，殺盡始安居，會得箇中意，鐵船水上浮。鐵船浮也，普請諸人各各洗脚上船，同入如來大圓覺海。風帆快便，說甚長期、短期？櫓棹不施，亦無得念、失念。無事扣舷歌一曲，有時和月載將歸，頭頭總是生涯，處處無非妙用。後園驢喫草，小魚吞大魚，者箇則且置，只如西院兩錯，畢竟作麼生商量？：任公把釣，蘇武牧羊。舉：德山示眾云：我先祖見處則不然，無佛、無祖。達磨大師是老臊胡，釋迦老子是乾屎橛，文殊、普賢者擔屎漢，等、妙二覺是破執凡夫，菩提

Senses.Explanation: The long is long of itself and the short is short of itself. Jiufeng Xiguang gives this answer when a visitor asks about the person within Jiufeng's landscape, after first asking about its streams and mountains. Huitang Zuxin uses the same line for the 'gathering in' side of a contrast with releasing a lone boat onto clear water. Yushan Shangsi strikes his staff, gives the pair, and then urges the assembly to see the root rather than remain among branches. The saying marks distinctions as they stand in each scene; none of these speakers offers a general theory of measurement.

Speaker: Zihu Lizong in an address to the assembly under the 子湖山第一代神力禪師語錄 heading. He urges strong trust in the saying that mind itself is Buddha and Dharma. Ancients who accepted it, he says, stayed in thatched huts or stone rooms to nurture the sacred embryo until the fruit of the Way matured; he asks why his listeners do not follow their example. Senses.Explanation: Nurturing the sacred embryo describes continued care and maturation after a decisive understanding, preserving the image of gestation. Langting Tingsui tells a head monk that the secluded phase must not become wasted time. Yuanwu Keqin places it beside eating and dressing in daily activity. Baohua Foci Pujian says quiet woods and water follow a breakthrough, while still requiring one more gate to be crossed. Mazu’s transmitted counsel likewise places it amid ordinary life; Furong Daokai applies it to stewards withdrawing from public office, and Zihu Lizong urges listeners to follow earlier practitioners into huts and stone rooms until the result ripens. These are distinct scenes, with the second Mazu recension and an actor-uncertain selected anthology passage excluded.

ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: 長鯨一吸海水盡，森森露出珊瑚枝

Senses.Explanation: With one gulp the great whale drains the sea, revealing dense branches of coral. An image of sweeping removal that brings hidden abundance to view. The source-backed uses include Juelang Daosheng in J25nB174, Fangrong Ruxi in J29nB249, Huijue Yi in J35nB340, Miyin Zhenchuan in J35nB343, and Jiguang Huo in J36nB367. Each is a current use of the full line. The image keeps its paired structure across the records. The line occurs in portraits and rites as well as case comments; the image is not a literal account of the sea.
